en: Preface to the Brief Outline of the General Discussion on the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* (with appended notes).
This sutra is extensive in its text and profound in its meaning. Previous commentaries merely divided the text into sections without fully extracting its underlying principles;
thus, the aim of its unified, pervasive doctrine was not fully elucidated, causing readers to follow the literal phrasing while the great meaning remained difficult to clarify. Consequently...
In practicing the three contemplations for cultivating the mind, one cannot find the gateway through which to enter.

Although lectures and expositions have circulated throughout the entire world from ancient times to the present, those who rely upon them to engage in cultivation all remain ignorant of their essential points. Thus, they fail the Tathāgata’s instruction on the path of correct practice.
Now, I, in my folly, venture to offer a comprehensive discussion, seeking directly to clarify the systematic principles so that students may grasp them at a single glance.
One will then perceive its ultimate aim. Its general outline merely first sets forth the essential meaning to reveal the intent beyond the literal text;

while its broad principles differ somewhat from those of previous scholars, the meaning is nonetheless clear and easy to perceive. Those who observe it must by no means rely on their own subjective conjectures.

Yet this has been neglected until now. I have therefore established headings and sub-sections for each chapter, assigning them titles and markers so that one may easily trace the currents and investigate their sources;
this is not merely a fondness for creating something novel. I hope you will not find this tedious.
I, the Elder of Mount Han, have arranged the sequence of these headings and sub-sections in advance to facilitate consultation while reading the text.
